summary: Venezuela admits citizens of the EU, the United Kingdom, Mexico and most of South America visa-free when they arrive by air, while everyone else, United States passport holders included, needs a tourist visa, which the Foreign Ministry now also issues electronically, and official travel advice is severe: the United Kingdom advises against all but essential travel and the United States says to reconsider travel, with both warning against any travel to the border regions.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months after the date you plan to leave Venezuela; visa applications also need 6 months' validity. Venezuela extended the validity of its own citizens' passports by decree, which some airlines and third countries do not accept — a separate problem, but one that affects dual nationals.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required of travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from Brazil, or who transited for more than 12 hours through an airport in Brazil. WHO also recommends vaccination for most travellers aged 9 months or over, except those staying only in Caracas, Valencia, Margarita Island and a few other low-risk areas.

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: Not an entry requirement. WHO reports high malaria risk all year in parts of Amazonas, Bolívar, Delta Amacuro and Sucre states, moderate risk in Zulia and low risk in Anzoátegui and Monagas, and recommends prevention in risk areas. Take advice from a travel clinic before any trip outside the main cities.

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not an entry requirement, but the US State Department highly recommends it, including medical evacuation cover: hospitals are short of medical staff, medicines and equipment. Read a policy's exclusions for Venezuela before you rely on it.

currencyLimits.text: Declare cash or travellers cheques worth USD 10,000 or more when you enter Venezuela; tax is charged on the excess. Goods worth more than USD 1,000, personal luggage included, must also be declared.

source.name: UK Foreign Office — Venezuela entry requirements

notes: The UK and Canada say you must declare goods, including personal luggage, worth more than USD 1,000, and that import tax may be due if the goods appear new.
Canada's travel advice says photographing sensitive installations, including the presidential palace, military sites, government buildings and airports, is prohibited.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says US dollars are widely accepted, that cash withdrawals from foreign bank accounts at ATMs are not possible, and that many ATMs don't accept international credit cards; carry small notes, and change money only at official exchange offices, as exchanging foreign currency outside authorized institutions is illegal. The UK says most local businesses accept bolívars, US dollars or international cards, though some card machines don't work with foreign cards.

safety.text: Official advice is severe. The UK advises against all travel within 80 km of the Colombian border and 40 km of the Brazilian and Guyanese borders, to Zulia state, the Orinoco Mining Arc and the area south of the Orinoco in Delta Amacuro, and against all but essential travel to the rest of the country. The United States rates Venezuela Level 3 (reconsider travel) for crime, kidnapping, terrorism and poor health care, and Level 4 (do not travel) for the Colombian border region, Amazonas, Apure, Táchira and Guárico states, Aragua outside Maracay and rural Bolívar. Violent crime, armed robbery and kidnapping occur; foreigners, including Europeans, have been detained and accused of terrorism, and arrivals can be held for hours or days for questioning. Power, water, fuel and medicine are often short, especially outside Caracas. After the June 2026 earthquakes La Guaira was declared a disaster zone under military control. Consular help is very limited.

tips.text: Check your own government's advice before doing anything else. The United States rates Venezuela Level 3 (reconsider travel), with Level 4 (do not travel) for the Colombian border region and several states, and the United Kingdom advises against all but essential travel to the country and against all travel to its border areas and Zulia. Travel insurance can be invalidated if you travel against your government's advice.

Venezuelan consular services in the United States have been suspended since 2019 and the US embassy in Caracas suspended operations in the same year; a phased resumption began in January 2026, but routine consular services remain suspended. US citizens apply for the Venezuelan visa electronically through the Foreign Ministry's portal, and US emergency help is not available outside Caracas if something goes wrong.

Bring US dollars in cash, in small notes. Canada's travel advice says dollars are widely accepted, that cash withdrawals from foreign bank accounts at ATMs are not possible and that you cannot rely on wire transfers for emergency funds.

Venezuela publishes no fixed visa-free stay: the days you are allowed are the ones written on your entry stamp and tourist card. Check them at the desk, because overstaying means problems at departure.

The UK advises against all travel within 80 km of the border with Colombia and within 40 km of the borders with Brazil and Guyana, says drug traffickers and illegal armed groups are active there, and advises against crossing between Venezuela and Colombia by land.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Venezuela?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Citizens of the EU and EEA, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Mexico and most South American countries enter visa-free for tourism when they arrive by air. Canadian and United States passport holders need a visa, as does everyone not on the Foreign Ministry's exemption list — including Chile, Peru, Panama, Cuba and the Dominican Republic. Apply online through the Foreign Ministry's Cancillería Digital portal, where the visa is sent by email, or at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate.

faq.question: Can US citizens travel to Venezuela?
faq.answer: It is legally possible but practically difficult. The US government says to reconsider travel (Level 3) and not to travel to the Colombian border region and several states. A visa is required, and Venezuelan consulates in the United States have been closed since 2019; since April 2026 the US Embassy in Caracas points US citizens to the Foreign Ministry's electronic visa, applied for online and sent by email. The US embassy in Caracas has not yet resumed full operations: routine consular services are suspended and emergency help is not available outside Caracas.

faq.question: How long can visa-free visitors stay in Venezuela?
faq.answer: Venezuela's Foreign Ministry publishes no fixed visa-free stay: its exemption list gives none. The UK government tells British visitors they can stay up to 90 days on a tourist card issued on arrival, and can apply at a SAIME office for an extension of up to 90 days before it expires. The officer writes the days granted on your entry stamp, so check it before leaving the counter.

faq.question: What money should I take to Venezuela?
faq.answer: US dollars in cash, in small notes. Canada's travel advice says US dollars are widely accepted, that cash withdrawals from foreign bank accounts at ATMs are not possible and that many ATMs don't accept international credit cards. The UK says most local businesses accept bolívars, US dollars or international cards, though some card machines don't work with foreign cards.

faq.question: Is Venezuela safe to visit?
faq.answer: No, not by ordinary standards. Violent crime, armed robbery and kidnapping occur, foreigners including Europeans have been detained and accused of terrorism, medicine, fuel and power are often short, and armed groups operate in the border states. The United Kingdom advises against all but essential travel to the country and the United States says to reconsider travel; travel insurance can be invalidated if you go against your government's advice.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Venezuela?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from Brazil: a certificate is required of travellers aged 1 or over coming from Brazil or after more than 12 hours' transit there. WHO also recommends vaccination for most of the country outside Caracas, Valencia and Margarita Island.
